reads.routing: (d) at HR-02 holds for the line at its strongest, not as worded. The duty's ground is the possible person's own good ("A person who would be glad to exist is harmed if we choose never to create them"), and his L3 reading sends that to HR-02 ("a move about the created person's own goods ends at HR-02"). But the redraft makes the total the duty's sufficient condition ("we ought to create them whenever that adds to the total good"), weighed across persons ("their interests are weighed with everyone's"), and by the same reading "a move about others' goods is met there". The via locus sinks agent-neutral aggregation ("indifferent to whose pleasure and whose pain are being summed"), and the (d) the route copies is the opponent who declines it ("decline the monster (the goods and harms fall on one person, not interpersonally)"). The record read the bound only against rights-future-generations#long. It read neither that horn nor population-ethics-paradoxes, which meets the bare total view ("devastating against Total utilitarianism, which must weigh aggregate welfare across populations"). The no-claimant (d) at rights-future-generations#long ends at HR-03, but on the library's side ("Only an asymmetry rescues one without the other."), so it does not move this line's bedrock.
reads.strongest_form: FAILS, narrowly, at the bound. The redraft cures SJ-003's defect: bounded, the duty no longer meets "The obligation would be literally infinite". But in the records V2b checked, Hare's total is a limit on the duty, not its trigger ("so long as this will increase the total satisfaction of preference"), and his population policy halts ("until the lowest segment of the population comes below the break-even point") with the shares held ("without altering its proportionate distribution"). Those two clauses are the ones the library's Mere Addition chain needs gone ("adding a person with positive but lower-than-average welfare"). Without them the bound keeps the chain open, and the card would meet a weaker argument than Hare makes.
reads.shape_not_surface: Passes, as SJ-003 found. Read further here: population-ethics-paradoxes' scholar line attacks the antinatalist's own axiology ("the world-destroyer conclusion"), not a duty to create, so the shape is not that node's objection.
reads.source: Partly. The weighing and the population policy are the article's (its reprint's opening: "the interests of that possible person have to be con sidered"). The golden-rule step, which the statement opens with, is Hare's in the records read only through the SEP's citations of 1975, 1988b and 1988c ("Abortion and the Golden Rule" first) and Chan 2004; neither places it in this article (RJ-007, RJ-009).
